body.heading: Blow a bubble
paragraphs: Dip your wand, blow gently, and watch a bubble float away. Look closely — every bubble you blow is a ball, never a cube or a star.
A bubble is a thin skin of soapy water wrapped around air. The skin pulls itself into the smallest, tightest shape it can — and that shape is a sphere.

body.heading: Colours on the skin
paragraphs: Hold a bubble up to the light. Colours slide and swirl on its surface, like oil on a puddle.
The colours come from light bouncing around in the bubble's thin skin. As the skin gets thinner, the colours change — then, pop.

body.heading: Bubble tricks
paragraphs: Blow a bubble onto a wet plate and it can sit there like a glass dome. Wet your wand and you can poke it gently into the bubble without popping it.
Dry things pop bubbles. Wet things let them live a little longer. That is the bubble-blower's secret.

takeaway: Bubbles are always round because their soapy skin pulls tight into the smallest shape — a sphere.
materials: Bubble mixture and wands (an adult provides)
safetyNotes: An adult should handle the bubble mixture. Blow bubbles away from faces, wipe up spills so nobody slips, and never drink bubble mixture.
screenFreeExtension: Try to catch a bubble on a wet hand without popping it.
